Let
\[
c=\cos\frac{\pi}{5},\qquad d=\cos\frac{2\pi}{5},\qquad
\Delta=\sqrt{1+2\rho+5\rho^2}.
\]
The largest possible value is
\[
\boxed{
\left(1+2c\rho+d(\Delta-1-\rho)\right)
\left(1-2d\rho-c(\Delta-1-\rho)\right)
\sqrt{\Delta-3\rho}
}.
\]

Here is the proof.

Let \(G=(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)\) be the Gram matrix. Then
\[
|\det[v_1\ \cdots\ v_5]|^2=\det G.
\]
Multiplying each \(v_i\) by a unit complex scalar does not change \(\det G\). Since
\[
\prod_{i=1}^5\langle v_i,v_{i+1}\rangle=-\rho^5,
\]
we may gauge the vectors so that
\[
\langle v_i,v_{i+1}\rangle=\alpha:=\rho e^{i\pi/5}
\]
for every \(i\), because \(\alpha^5=-\rho^5\).

Now maximize \(\det G\) among positive definite Hermitian matrices with diagonal entries \(1\) and cyclic adjacent entries \(\alpha\). The function \(\log\det G\) is strictly concave, so the maximizer is unique. Cyclic symmetry forces the maximizer to be circulant. Thus it has first row
\[
(1,\alpha,\gamma,\overline{\gamma},\overline{\alpha}).
\]
A reflection symmetry combined with a gauge transformation forces
\[
\gamma=s e^{2\pi i/5}
\]
with \(s\in\mathbb R\).

The eigenvalues of this circulant matrix are
\[
A=1+2c\rho+2ds \quad \text{with multiplicity }2,
\]
\[
B=1-2d\rho-2cs \quad \text{with multiplicity }2,
\]
and
\[
C=1-2\rho+2s \quad \text{with multiplicity }1.
\]
Hence
\[
\det G=A^2B^2C.
\]

So we maximize
\[
A^2B^2C
\]
over the interval where \(A,B,C>0\). Differentiating \(\log(A^2B^2C)\) gives
\[
\frac{4d}{A}-\frac{4c}{B}+\frac{2}{C}=0.
\]
Using
\[
cd=\frac14,\qquad c-d=\frac12,\qquad c^2+d^2=\frac34,
\]
this reduces to
\[
s^2+(1+\rho)s-\rho^2=0.
\]
The admissible root is
\[
s=\frac{\Delta-1-\rho}{2},
\qquad
\Delta=\sqrt{1+2\rho+5\rho^2}.
\]
Then
\[
C=1-2\rho+2s=\Delta-3\rho>0
\]
because \(\rho<\cos(\pi/5)\). Substituting this \(s\) into \(A,B,C\), we get
\[
|\det[v_1\ \cdots\ v_5]|
=\sqrt{\det G}
=AB\sqrt C,
\]
which is exactly
\[
\boxed{
\left(1+2\rho\cos\frac{\pi}{5}
+\cos\frac{2\pi}{5}\bigl(\sqrt{1+2\rho+5\rho^2}-1-\rho\bigr)\right)
\left(1-2\rho\cos\frac{2\pi}{5}
-\cos\frac{\pi}{5}\bigl(\sqrt{1+2\rho+5\rho^2}-1-\rho\bigr)\right)
\sqrt{\sqrt{1+2\rho+5\rho^2}-3\rho}
}.
\]
